articles.content:
What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life?

For Robert Pattinson , there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. He spent it, rather predictably, watching an arthouse horror film. His longtime friend and collaborator Robert Eggers told Variety this week that Pattinson was screening the director’s forthcoming genre drama “Werwulf” when the Bond news broke. Nothing like a stark naked Aaron Taylor-Johnson terrorizing a quaint village to pass the time. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But after months (years, really) of toiling and speculation over who would replace Daniel Craig in the film adaptations of Ian Fleming’s spy novels, Pattinson took the crown. It buttons up a delicious, messy and very public guessing game over which lucky man would land the iconic role. When Amazon MGM bought out rights to James Bond from longtime custodians the Broccoli family in 2025, intentions were set for a young star who could shoulder the franchise for a decade or two. An A-list team of producers (Amy Pascal of “Spider-Man” and David Heyman of the “Harry Potter” movies) recruited Denis Villeneuve to direct. Together, with significant influence from Amazon execs Courtenay Valenti and Mike Hopkins (and yes, Jeff Bezos), they screen-tested a laundry list of virile performers — including Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor — earlier this year.

For the curious, the batch of screen tests cost Amazon MGM between $300,000 and $500,000 to pull off, ostensibly in secret (everyone found out), sources familiar with the process say. But two wildcard actors who tested at the last minute — “Superman” star Nicholas Hoult and the DCU’s reining Batman, Pattinson — tipped the scales. Villeneuve’s voice became the most trusted in the room on the matter of Bond’s casting, two insiders tell Variety . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

His shorthand with Pattinson from working on “Dune: Part Three” made the choice inevitable, according to industry insiders — especially after Turner, the early favorite, came under scrutiny against more established names like Hoult and Pattinson. Lowden, the heat-seeking star of “Slow Horses,” was even the subject of a suspected sabotage campaign when paparazzi footage circulated showed the actor bungling an on-set motorcycle stunt just two weeks before the Bond casting was confirmed.

A sect of the internet lost its mind when Variety reported earlier this month that Harry Styles and Theo James were both in talks for the role. It’s rare, even by tentpole movie standards, that such a long list of candidates would flow so freely through public channels. The studios hate it because it makes them seem indecisive, one exec says. Talent absolutely hates it because the also-rans will have to answer for almost being James Bond on talk show couches and podcasts for the next 10 years.

“Whatever, it’s really fun,” one top talent rep tells Variety of the audition merry-go-round.

While there will be detractors, it’s inarguable that the Bond gig now enshrines Pattinson in the upper echelons of movie stardom. He was already well on his way, with even civilian social media pundits having commented on the “generational run” Pattinson has been living out onscreen in films like “Primetime,” “The Odyssey,” “The Drama,” “Die My Love” and, obviously, “The Batman.” That’s to say nothing of the deeply indie era (“Good Time,” “The Lighthouse”) that followed major franchise moments like his star-making turn in the “Twilight Saga” movies and a prominent role in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.” The new job also represents a major win for Pattinson’s agent of more than 20 years, Stephanie Ritz of WME. Ritz and team have managed to populate massive IP with Pattinson’s face while still allowing the actor to take risks and brand himself a maverick for the cross-generational devotees of studios like A24.

Given the shocking November news that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran had been jettisoned by the David Ellison regime, it’s doubtful Pattinson would linger long as Matt Reeves’ caped crusader — freeing him up to embody the sultry British charm and execute the bare-knuckle action audiences have come to expect from 007. Art-house horror movies may have to take a back seat.

articles.title: Cartoon Network Changed Superheroes With This '90s Hit, But Its Place in Animation History Is Forgotten

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Cartoon Network has been an icon of animation history since its launch in 1992, with it releasing popular shows throughout the decades like Dexter's Laboratory , Samurai Jack , Ben 10 , Adventure Time , and more. One of the company's most beloved shows just celebrated its anniversary, reminding viewers of one of Cartoon Network's earliest and best original series.

Superheroes have been a staple of Cartoon Network since the beginning , from acquired programming like Super Friends to original shows like Teen Titans Go! . However, it is impossible to deny that their most famous superhero series is Craig McCracken's 1998 masterpiece, The Powerpuff Girls .

While a student at the California Institute of the Arts, Craig McCracken developed a series titled Whoopass Stew! , a parody of the superhero shows of the 1960s that followed three little girls who are granted extraordinary powers when the professor accidentally adds a can of whoopass to his experiment. The short, titled "A Sticky Situation," was well-received enough to land McCracken a pitch meeting at Hanna-Barbera. After the project was reworked as The Powerpuff Girls , two shorts were produced for Cartoon Network's World Premiere Toons block. The first of these, "Meat Fuzzy Lumpkins," aired on February 20, 1995, while the second, "Crime 101," aired on January 28, 1996. Unfortunately, the shorts didn't get picked up for a series, and McCracken went on to work for Genndy Tartakovsky on Dexter's Laboratory . While there, McCracken was then allowed to pitch The Powerpuff Girls again, and in 1997, the series was greenlit.

On November 18, 1998, The Powerpuff Girls premiered on Cartoon Network, with the premiere consisting of the segments "Monkey See, Doggie Do" and "Mommy Fearest." The show was a hit, with it being the highest-rated premiere of a Cartoon Network series at the time of its airing. The show received incredible viewership numbers across children and adult audiences, something that surprised the network due to the show being designed to appeal to young viewers. However, the series' critical and commercial success allowed it to run for six seasons, and the series ended on March 25, 2005, with the release of its 78th episode.

The Powerpuff Girls has become an icon of animation, allowing its influence to far outlast the show's original run. The franchise has come back for several other projects, including the 2002 The Powerpuff Girls Movie and the 2006 anime Powerpuff Girls Z . Two specials have been produced since the show's cancellation, such as the half-hour 2009 episode "The Powerpuff Girls Rule!!!" and the 2014 CGI special Powerpuff Girls: Dance Pantsed . Most interestingly, a live-action sequel series was in development at The CW, starring Chloe Bennet, Dove Cameron, and Yana Perrault as Blossom, Bubbles, and Buttercup, respectively. However, the series was cancelled before release due to negative reviews.

The Powerpuff Girls has maintained its popularity more than two decades after the show's cancellation, with merchandise and memes spawned from the franchise still being all over the place. It could be argued that The Powerpuff Girls is Cartoon Network's most iconic show of all time, with it helping to define the channel's original programming in its early days and influencing the entire field of animation.

The Powerpuff Girls is a historic show for many reasons, but one of the show's most notable facts is rarely discussed. Hanna-Barbera Productions, named for founders William Hanna and Joseph Barbera, helped create the field of television animation in the early 1950s and 60s. Shows like The Huckleberry Hound Show , The Flintstones , Scooby-Doo, Where Are You? , and more are still well-known today , having become some of the company's most popular programs. However, The Powerpuff Girls often isn't lumped in with these Hanna-Barbera programs, despite the fact that it was a Hanna-Barbera Show.

The Powerpuff Girls was the final Hanna-Barbera series to premiere, with its first four seasons being produced by the company. Seasons 5 and 6 were produced by Cartoon Network Studios after Hanna-Barbera was absorbed into Warner Bros. Animation in 2001. This makes The Powerpuff Girls a milestone in the history of animation, with it marking the end of the Hanna-Barbera era and the beginning of Cartoon Network. It is hard to deny the impact that the show has had since its premiere, and it is still beloved by many 28 years after its started.

articles.content:
Rich Eisen came out on to the set of his long-running talk show the other day, only to find Bono from U2 doing an impression of the running-man logo that has long been a part of the program's identifying marks. When Eisen went to take part, he discovered the person taking pictures of the encounter wasn't the program's staff photographer, but rather The Edge.

Eisen calls it being "stuck in a moment I didn't want to get out of." And that's the last U2 song joke we'll make here. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Kennedy Center Sets 2026 Honorees: David Mamet, Paul Anka, Andy Garcia and More Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Sam Fender and Cher to Headline Glastonbury Festival

The host has long been known for his sportscasting and "The Rich Eisen Show" has long been featured as part of sports programming, but that doesn't mean the host and the program can't take a detour once in a while.

"This is what our show is about. It's a pop culture show," Eisen says during a recent interview. "Sports is just one spoke on the pop culture wheel." U2 holds forth with Eisen on Friday's program.

Eisen has over the years talked with Jon Bon Jovi, Jodie Foster, James Taylor, Will Ferrell, Kenny Chesney and Snoop Dogg, and there are reasons for him to do so. Since returning to the ESPN empire (Eisen was an ESPN regular between 1996 and 2003), Eisen's show now streams on Disney+ and the ESPN App, among other venues.

"We are exposed to a much larger audience of movies, television, music and sports fans," says Eisen, adding: We put the word out 12 years ago that, yes, we are on sports talk radio, and yues, I'm known certain in my other jobs as a sportscaster, but I'm just as into movies and music and TV shows and live theater as anybody else." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

How did Eisen's team land U2? The band, which just released its first full album, Carnaval de Luz, in nine years, is scheduled to play the halftime show of Netflix's stream of a Thanksgiving Eve game taking place between the Green Day Packers and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. That's not too far from the studio that houses Eisen's show. A producer called. The band's publicist seemed willing.

Eisen says he didn't spend hours trying to come up with questions that would ferret out some small detail that fans don't already know. Instead, his focus is on trying to create "a good hang."

"The way I approach it is just to ask them questions that I'm curious to know the answers to," the host says. "If I somehow unearth something that hasn't been talked about, then so be it." Eisen and his staff have devised a Q&A segment that plays well on YouTube in which he asks guests to confirm or knock down stories and memes about them that are already at play in the digi-sphere. The exchanges, he says, are popular.

The "Eisen" team hopes for more. "We take the show seriously but we don't take ourselves seriously," says Eisen. "We are open for business every day."

articles.title: Prince Harry Approves of Robert Pattinson's Bond Casting
articles.summary: "I want to make sure it's in good hands," said the Duke of Sussex, making his first daytime television appearance since moving back to Britain with Meghan Markle, Prince Archie and Prince Lilibet.

Prince Harry made a surprise appearance on British daytime television on Friday, where he gave incoming 007 Robert Pattinson the royal seal of approval.

In his first appearance on ITV's This Morning since moving back to the U.K., the Duke of Sussex was asked about Monday's news that Pattinson has been tapped to succeed Daniel Craig as James Bond in the new film from Amazon MGM Studios .

"I think it's great," said Harry to hosts Alison Hammond and Dermot O'Leary about the casting news. "I can't wait to see it." BTS won the coveted Artist of the Year category for the eighth time, and Enhypen won three: Fans' Choice of the Year, Favorite M-Countdown Stage and Fan's Choice Top 10 - Male. Ive won Best Female Group.

The music event, which broadcasts in Korea on Mnet , brings together Korean music performers from across generations over two nights.

The awards have benefitted from the explosion in interest in Korean culture. Having started as domestic awards ceremony in 1999, MAMA became the first K-pop ceremony to be held overseas, and in 2024 it also took place in the U.S. for the first time. "MAMA Awards has grown alongside K-POP’s global growth, we believe these efforts have created more ways for artists and fans around the world to connect," said Yoon Shin Hye, who is head of CJ ENM -owned Mnet.

“Over the past 27 years, MAMA Awards has expanded its stages to places it had never been, connected artists and fans in ways never seen before, and been the first to show K-pop’s new possibilities," added Harry H.K. Shin, Head of Music Entertainment at CJ ENM in a statement. "All of that was possible with our one firm belief: 'Music Makes One.'

"This year, we want to once again deliver an experience where people connect through music, beyond the boundaries of time and space, generation and region."

The awards come at an important juncture for K-pop music. The global glare has put K-pop under the microscope and a recent New York Times article about restrictions within artist contracts caused major debate, prompting the K-pop music association to hit back and defend the industry. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The South Korean government earlier this week said it would undertake a survey to assess how underage performers were treated. Asked about the health of K-pop, Yoon said the industry relied on finding new successes, and, "For that to happen, the creativity of everyone who makes music, not just the artists but also the songwriters, producers, choreographers, directors and creators, needs to be respected."

Yoon was keen the point to the unifying nature of the awards for fans. "At MAMA Awards, they can discover the same songs, share what they like and connect through music. What we want to show through this year’s theme, 'a music interstellar,' is fans from different generations and different parts of the world coming together and discovering new moments."

Here's an interview with Yoon conducted before to night's ceremony.

DEADLINE: What scale of investment does the event take to organise?

Yoon Shin Hye : MAMA Awards is much more than an awards ceremony. It’s a major global project that brings together CJ ENM’s music, broadcasting and global network, along with its production capabilities. I can’t disclose specific figures, but it takes experts across many fields and a lot of infrastructure. Everything from creative planning, stage production and direction to cutting-edge technology, global live broadcasting and on-site operations goes into bringing each artist’s performance to life.

And because MAMA Awards has to reflect each year’s K-pop’s trends and where the industry is heading, we start preparing at the very beginning of the year. Throughout the year, we meet fans through M Countdown , our Mnet weekly K-POP chart show, and KCON, our K-Pop festival in places like Japan and the U.S. All of that leads up to MAMA AWARDS, where global fandoms come together as one. So really, MAMA is the result of a year-long journey.

DEADLINE: What are you trying to show the world with this event?

YSH: We truly believe music can bring people together, regardless of language, nationality, culture or generation. MAMA Awards is where artists and fans from all over the world get to experience that together. Mnet, which hosts the awards, started as a music channel in 1995 and turned 30 last year. Over those three decades, we’ve grown up alongside generations of K-pop, introducing artists’ music and performances and bringing them closer to fans worldwide. MAMA Awards has been part of that journey, growing with K-Pop and becoming a global stage where artists meet fans around the world.

DEADLINE: What are the highlights of the event and can you hint at any surprises?

YSH: This year, I’d say the thing to look out for is performances and collaborations that cross generations, genres and cultures. First, you’ll see different generations of K-Pop on one stage. There’s Panic, the legendary Korean duo celebrating 31 years since their debut in 1995, and BIGBANG marking their 20th anniversary. And alongside them, artists who debuted at every point from the early 2000s right up to 2026.

We’ve also got some exciting projects where K-pop meets global entertainment: Enhypehm teaming up with Dune: Part Three for MAMA Awards' signature Cinematic Stage, which brings the film’s world into a K-pop performance. And BIGBANG is pairing up with Dooly the Little Dinosaur, a much-loved Korean animated character, for a collaboration no one will see coming.

articles.title: Andrea Scrosati to Leave Fremantle Group
articles.summary: As Fremantle Group COO and CEO of Continental Europe, Scrosati oversaw Fremantle's international expansion into feature films and TV drama, including the acquisition of Element Pictures ('Poor Things', 'Normal People') and Lux Vide ('Medici').
articles.content:
Fremantle Group COO and CEO Continental Europe Andrea Scrosati is stepping down after an eight-year tenure in which he oversaw an ambitious expansion of the Fremantle's international production operations, including the acquisition of multiple independent film and TV production companies.

Fremantle announced Friday that Scrosati, who joined the company from Sky Italia in 2018, and was named CEO Continental Europe in 2021, is stepping down to pursue a new entrepreneurial venture. He will stay on until the end of January 2027 to support the transition to new leadership.

During his tenure, Scrosati led Fremantle’s mergers and acquisitions strategy, transforming the company from a business primarily associated with international entertainment formats into a global production group with a substantial presence in premium drama, independent film and documentaries.

Among the most significant acquisitions included Dublin-based Element Pictures, the production company behind The Favourite , Room and Normal People ; Italian producer Lux Vide, whose credits include Medici , Leonardo and Devils ; and the Asacha Media Group, which owns eight production labels across France, Italy, including Red Planet Pictures, the British producer of Death in Paradise , and Italy’s Picomedia.

The acquisitions also provided the foundation for Fremantle’s expansion in film. Among the major productions backed during Scrosati’s tenure were Yorgos Lanthimos’ Poor Things ; Joanna Hogg’s The Eternal Daughter ; Ali Abbasi’s The Apprentice ; and Sebastián Lelio’s The Wonder . During Scrosati's tenure, Fremantle racked up 17 Oscar nominations and four Academy Awards for its titles.

Scrosati also oversaw Fremantle’s expansion into documentaries and sports programing, the growth of its free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channel business and the creation of Imaginae Studios, a standalone production label focused on artificial intelligence. Its first production, Art Awakens , launched in 2026.

The M&A activity was part of a broader growth strategy set by Fremantle's parent company RTL Group, which in 2021 set an ambitious target of doubling Fremantle’s annual revenue to €3 billion ($3.3 billion) within four years, through acquisitions and the expansion of Fremantle’s production businesses. The company did not reach that goal. Revenue peaked at approximately €2.27 billion in 2023 before falling to €2.254 billion in 2024 and €2.043 billion in 2025, leaving it nearly €1 billion short of the original target. RTL has subsequently pushed the €3 billion ambition further into the future.

"Andrea has made an enormous contribution to Fremantle over the past eight years," Jennifer Mullin, Global CEO Fremantle, said in a statement. "He has been instrumental in our growth and transformation, from helping build Fremantle into a true portfolio company and leading our M&A strategy, to establishing our film strategy and constantly pushing us to think differently about innovation and the future of our business."

Scrosati said the time was right to move on and focus on building something new. “I leave with enormous pride in what we have achieved together and great affection for the company and everyone who makes it what it is."

articles.title: One Big Complaint About The Voice I Always Remember I Have With The Live Shows
articles.summary: Please bring back the coach banter and shenanigans on The Voice.
articles.content:
The level of talent on Season 30 of NBC’s long-running singing competition The Voice , currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule , is undeniable. The cuts have been "brutal, " and some really incredible singers already went home before the Live Shows even started. The success of the show isn’t solely about the contestants. We also tune in to for the fun coach interactions, all of which has been noticeably absent during the live performances, disappointingly so.

Earlier this season, Kelly Clarkson and newbie Riley Green really upped The Voice coach prank game . Whether it was a personalized gift from the American Idol winner attempting to help a fellow coach get over losing top-notch singers during the Blind Auditions, or it was the country music superstar using his duck call for a laugh, those moments have been glaringly lacking from the Live Shows.

With the Blind Auditions, Battles, and Cut Week having two-hour episodes, cutting the Live Shows to one hour doesn’t even allow for much coach commentary and feedback. To me that's a big problem. When it comes time to announce which singers have made it through for another week and who’s going to be sent home, there’s barely the time to even say goodbye, right?

articles.title: 5 Most Exciting GTA 6 Easter Eggs Players Have Found After Launch Day
articles.summary: Courtesy of Rockstar Games There are Easter Eggs in every Rockstar game, but Grand Theft Auto 6 might have the most secrets yet, including tons of secrets for players to track down in its massive world. Everything hasn't been discovered yet soon after the game's launch, but some fans have discovered fascinating content that goes outside the grounded or […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There are Easter Eggs in every Rockstar game, but Grand Theft Auto 6 might have the most secrets yet, including tons of secrets for players to track down in its massive world. Everything hasn't been discovered yet soon after the game's launch, but some fans have discovered fascinating content that goes outside the grounded or "normal" references featured in other parts of the title. Instead of references to past GTA settings or stories, there are outlandish and downright bizarre Easter Eggs in some places that continue Rockstar's tradition of strange secrets in their open-world experiences.

Players are still finding secrets in Red Dead Redemption 2 , so it'll likely be years before every corner of GTA 6 has been similarly pried for information. That being said, players have already been uncovering plenty of Easter Eggs for GTA 6 that pay homage to secrets of past titles in the series, as well as some new ones implemented by Rockstar. From larger connections to popular shows or movies to various jokes and winks toward the audience, Rockstar has outdone themselves with the Easter Egg quality present in this game.

One Easter Egg most players may have already found is a truly surprising scene of a dog driving a jet ski out into the oceans of GTA 6 as you're swimming. You might be scuba diving, driving a jet ski yourself, or simply exploring beyond beach shores before this dog pulls up next to you in a random encounter. Whether you're Jason or Lucia, you can question this dog, but they aren't exactly going to provide any answers right away. Instead, you can hop into the jet ski with the dog, and travel across the waves in style as you see some beautiful scenery through their capable paws.

Sticking with the dog will have you travel all along the coastal parts of Leonida, but the Leondia Keys is mainly where you'll find this Easter Egg the most. While not guaranteed in that zone, it has the most water to work with, and is host to the dog's home — a small island off the coast where other canines are playing together. It seems like a bunch of dogs have created their own secret hideout of sorts, with multiple dogs there with life jackets, sunglasses, and otherwise cool clothing that lets you know what kind of club they run.

The jet ski dog will eventually take you to their island if you stick with them, where you can play with the dogs there until you want to leave. This isn't a very layered Easter Egg, but it does break up the usual sights of Vice City in GTA 6 with something you aren't likely to expect. Accessing Photo mode when this happens is almost a must, as this rare ride along with arguably the smoothest character in GTA 6 is something that only takes place once.

Players can find an actual cryptid in GTA 6 , mirroring the appearance of other strange creatures that have shown up in past games throughout the franchises. Games like GTA: San Andreas created an Easter Egg with the Loch Ness monster, while other titles had other wild figures like the "Ratman," or even Bigfoot themselves. A tall, wild Bigfoot is the most famous American cryptid, but it shows up in GTA 6 as something you can see and chase down yourself. However, it is named the "Skunk Ape" in GTA 6 , for the trail of mysterious gas it seems to emit as it moves around.

This large, hairy, bipedal cousin of Bigfoot creature can be located around in Grassrivers area of the map, again showing up as a random encounter. There are several shrines and effigies scattered around this area showing some sort of worship toward the Skunk Ape, typically made out of straw and rope in the forests there. By hanging around a Skunk Ape shrine, the creature might pop up unexpectedly, being something you can chase into the woods until the gas it creates eventually knocks your character out. You should be able to see the Skunk Ape hunting and feeding on local wildlife like deer, making it easier to hear and spot.

Even if you don't go unconscious from chasing the Skunk Ape, the creature has some sort of weird power that allows it to turn into a tree or simply vanish from sight. At some point in your pursuit, the cryptid will vanish, leaving behind nothing. That being said, there are quests in the game tied to spotting this creature, starting with early sightings with Jason as he explores the areas where the Skunk Ape could appear. By talking to the NPC Kirk, a cryptid hunter, you should be able to turn this chase into something that grants a few rewards.

The fictional series Dexter is about a serial killer in a bay area, in a location very similar to the Florida-inspired region of Leonida that GTA 6 takes place in. The Bay Harbor Butcher may be alive and well in GTA 6 through a recently found Easter Egg within Vice City, the largest area in the game. There is an apartment complex in the Washington Island sub-area of Vice City, close to the marked spots for Vice Beach Top Fun Drones and Pay N' Spray, two vendor locations. From here, going northeast from Penmarch Isle should take you to a series of buildings named Trinity Apartments, which may alert Dexter fans.

The Trinity Killer was one of the most notorious villains from Season 4 of Dexter , so players should be drawn to the GTA 6 apartments possibly referencing the other serial killer. Going to one of the upper corner apartment buildings here will show a room with all of its shades shuttered, in an eerie contrast to the other residents near that space. By going to the roof of the building, you can find all of Dexter Morgan's gear, including a series of syringes he uses to knock out his soon-to-be victims. Here, you can also find a knife, some rope, gloves, multiple tool boxes, a rag, and some handcuffs indicating the killer's "process."

In the distance from the roof, you may also spot a boot that looks similar to Dexter's "Slice of Life" vessel, making the Easter Egg even more complete than you would think. This second floor space is not one to interact with as much as the jet ski dog or Skunk Ape, but it does provide a nice homage to another series with a similar aesthetic to the game. With fan theories already pointing toward the character Mandy as being a possible serial killer herself, the Dexter references make even more sense as you play.

Believe it or not, aliens have always been a part of the Grand Theft Auto series, existing as Easter Eggs ever since GTA 3 and San Andreas with rumors and myths about UFO sightings. GTA 6 , on the other hand, has Rockstar finally give the alien rumors more attention than just a UFO on a poster card or a fleeting encounter with the extraterrestrial as seen in games like GTA 5 . In this game, players can actually get abducted by aliens, even getting a chance to travel inside a UFO should they control the right character during that situation. That being said, players first have to observe an abduction happening, which is easier said than done.

By going outside in Port Gellhorn, an area of the Leonida map, at 2am or later might trigger a random encounter, where you can see a bright light up in the sky. Running toward it might let you catch a glimpse of a woman being abducted by aliens, floating upward before your presence may stop the process. During that same night, you'll be abducted next, with events afterward changing based on if you're playing as Jason or Lucia. Depending on who you are, the following events can take place:

The research facility Jason can travel to is abandoned, and located in Pelican Valley to the southeast, getting close to the borders of Mariana County. Breaking into this place isn't hard, but it does take a special code that you can only find from one of the military airfields in the game, which raises your wanted level fast in GTA 6 by trespassing. The code is 2-3-4-1, and opens up the bunker full of dead cows and scientists, but traveling through this area reveals research about those studying the aliens. Eventually, you can put a glass of milk from the facility into a canister of some kind, to reveal a living alien people had captured.

You can then carry this alien out of the facility, where a short cutscene will show the UFO coming back and taking the little gray creature back to its people. This interaction will greatly increase your stats and grant experience, even though it isn't tied to a specific quest like the one revolving around the Skunk Ape. At the same time, this is one of the wildest things that can take place in GTA 6 , even earning you the "The Truth is Out There" achievement as a nice little nod to The X-Files show.

Perhaps the most on-the-nose Easter Egg in GTA 6 is found at the top of a tower in South Vice-Dale County, which is arguably the highest point in the game. Climbing to the top of a radio tower in this area takes a considerable amount of time, but Rockstar seems to appreciate the effort, as players are rewarded with a literal nest of eggs at the top. These "Easter Eggs" are named as such, acting as brightly colored eggs that look like they would be hidden during the titular holiday. Throwing one of these Easter Eggs off the tower will actually trigger a special cutscene, where it hits someone's windshield to hilarious results.

There are other Easter Eggs that players are finding besides this one too, including an encounter with a Giant Crab that is sparse in details at this time of writing. References to past GTA games also combine with connections to Rockstar's other games, like the Red Dead Redemption series. Multiple parodies exist within the game too, with X-Men knock-offs and other shows being spoofed on TV should you sit down and watch something. GTA 6 is a game that will likely keep adding Easter Eggs as new updates come and go, making it a content-rich title players will be exploring for years.

What are some of your favorite Easter Eggs in GTA 6 so far? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: FromSoftware Needs to Bring Its Most Underrated Game Back and a New Indie Masterpiece Proves It
articles.summary: FromSoftware is one of gaming's most recognizable names, largely because of the addictive difficulty of its games. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google FromSoftware is one of gaming's most recognizable names, largely because of the addictive difficulty of its games. Dark Souls and Elden Ring have given it widespread acclaim, while Bloodborne remains one of the most beloved titles of all time. Even now, fans eagerly await its Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods . However, some of FromSoftware's most interesting ideas haven't been explored in decades. And one recent indie developer shows just how influential those games were and how they can capture the same success as FromSoftware's soulslike entries, especially considering they were responsible for the genre's creation.

King's Field is one of FromSoftware's most underrated games and largely helped the soulslike genre form. Yet, despite how important it is, the series has all but disappeared. That is until indie developer Freshly Baked Games released Queen's Domain . The reception from reviewers and players has been incredible, showing that there is still an audience for this type of dungeon crawler. It is also a strong argument that FromSoftware should return to King's Field and revive one of its legacy franchises with modern hardware and standards.

Long before FromSoftware became known for its punishing boss fights, it proved it could create immersive and engaging fantasy worlds with King's Field . Released in 1994 for the original PlayStation, King's Field was FromSoftware's first video game. It established many of the characteristics the studio is known for, such as oppressive environments, cryptic storytelling, unforgiving enemies, and minimal guidance. Even the Moonlight Sword, which has appeared throughout FromSoftware's history in various forms, was first introduced here.

The influence of King's Field on the soulslike genre is something Hidetaka Miyazaki himself has acknowledged. While Demon's Souls wasn't developed as a sequel, it certainly feels like an expanded version of the formula. There are clear similarities between the games, particularly in how they encourage players to overcome challenges through patience, experimentation, and knowledge of their surroundings rather than overwhelming enemies with brute force.

One of my favorite things about FromSoftware's RPGs is their storytelling, particularly how the environment contributes to this. There is something special about standing outside a dark tunnel, debating whether whatever treasure lies inside is worth risking your progress and life. King's Field capitalized on that feeling through its first-person perspective, creating a degree of vulnerability that distinguishes it from modern soulslike games. Unfortunately, the series hasn't received a mainline entry since King's Field IV in 2001.

But on October 30th, 2026, King's Field fans got the next best thing in Queen's Domain . Players explore the mysterious Isle of Neasied while searching for their missing father, discovering secrets, collecting weapons, and battling monsters. Its retro graphics, stamina-based combat, and labyrinthine environments make it feel immediately like King's Field , but this isn't just nostalgia bait. The game is genuinely incredible and deserves all its praise.

But the game isn't just copying FromSoftware. Queen's Domain gives players the Holy Sword Endu, which does more than just slay enemies. It gives players aerial movement abilities that transform how they explore environments, almost leaning into a Metroidvania feel. Revisiting locations after gaining upgrades unveils new secrets and keeps players on their toes. Progression across Queen's Domain is incredibly rewarding and goes beyond just being influenced by FromSoftware and creating its own identity.

The reception speaks for itself. Freshly Baked Games announced that Queen's Domain sold 100,000 copies within five days of release. It also boasts an Overwhelmingly Positive rating on Steam across 5,600 reviews. The appeal of this style of game cannot be understated enough. Other games like this have come and gone, such as Dread Delusion , but Queen's Domain demanded attention, and it has absolutely received it.

FromSoftware returning to an older franchise wouldn't be a surprise. Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon revived the series in 2023 after nearly a decade of being dormant. Rather than forcing its soulslike formula onto the franchise, FromSoftware kept the game to its series' roots while implementing modern elements from its current franchises. This is absolutely the direction a new King's Field game has to go, and it is past time that we receive a new game in this cult classic series.

Exploring an interconnected kingdom with the environmental detail of Elden Ring , the unsettling atmosphere of Bloodborne , and the first-person exploration of King's Field . Valor Mortis proved a first-person soulslike could work , but FromSoftware can take this to another level. The studio's responsive combat, sophisticated enemy behavior, expanded magic systems, and environmental puzzles with a King's Field name would be a dream come true.

Sadly, FromSoftware and Miyazaki have expressed reservations about reviving King's Field , though this was back in 2016. But Queen's Domain is a great example of why revisiting the past and taking risks is important. FromSoftware should not abandon soulslike games, but it has the bandwidth and resources to diversify its library. A new King's Field is the perfect way to do that, and it would even minimize the risk considering the series has an established foundation.

Archie Renaux is hesitant to call his character in War a villain. Johnny, the ambitious (often to a fault) junior lawyer who plays a double-agent litigator in the slick divorce drama, is often the one called upon to do the dirty work: the double-crossing, the manipulating of both witnesses and plaintiffs, and then, of course, the whole business of being a mole. "He does awful things, but he's a puppet more so than anything else," says Renaux. "He's been taken advantage of, really."

The series, from George Kay ( Lupin ), follows two rival London firms — the white-shoe Cathcarts and the newer, scrappier Taylor & Byrne — as they represent a tech mogul (played by Dominic West ) and an actress ( Sienna Miller ) at the tumultuous end of their marriage. Renaux's Johnny ostensibly works for Taylor & Byrne, but has been promised an eventual job at Cathcarts in exchange for double-crossing information about the high-profile case. Throughout the season, we see him cheating on his girlfriend with Miller's Carla and framing a fellow junior lawyer after he's almost caught with compromising inside intel. What do you remember about the audition process for the show?

I was on another job and we were doing night shoots in Canada, and I got an email about the audition but it was so hectic that I didn't feel like I could afford to give my attention to anything else. articles.title: Harrison Ford Kisses Calista Flockhart On Stage As Couple Receives Their First Joint Award
articles.summary: Flockhart revealed the reason they said yes to the honor before joking that her other half didn't need convincing: "Between you and me, Harrison complains that he doesn't get enough attention."
articles.content:
When Women's Guild Cedars-Sinai reached out to ask Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart if they would join forces to accept a Hollywood Icon Award at the Stardust Ball, the organization got a quick answer.

"We didn't hesitate. We said yes. We said yes, yes, yes ," Flockhart revealed while standing next to her husband on a ballroom stage inside at Beverly Wilshire, A Four Seasons Hotel on Wednesday night. "And I promise you, it was not because we wanted an award. Well, actually maybe [Harrison] did. Between you and me, Harrison complains that he doesn't get enough attention. But really, it's true. I'm not joking." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Lifestyle Harrison Ford Joins Greg Berlanti, Goldie Hawn and Melissa McCarthy as Paley Gala Honorees Business Byron Allen Sells His Stake in Starz

Judging by the look on Ford's face, it was hard to tell if Flockhart was teasing. articles.title: 'The Body' Breakout Geena Meszaros on Finding Empathy for Lisbeth and "Life-Altering" Female Friendships

articles.content:
Actress Geena Meszaros has been galavanting around Hollywood the last few weeks, arm-in-arm with her fellow young actresses from The Body . But a month ago, she was back home in Canada, fresh off some October snow, finding herself in limbo.

Meszaros has been patiently waiting for the Netflix coming-of-age series centered around the dance team at a Catholic school to come out since it wrapped filming earlier this year after six months of shooting. In the week since it's landed on the streamer, the internet, and the Hollywood party crowds, can't get enough of the show's talented gang of young actresses. "I don't think I was even submitted for it," she tells The Hollywood Reporte r of how she came to join the project. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Netflix Renews Japanese Crime Hit 'Tokyo Swindlers' for Season 2 TV Nikki Glaser Signs Deal With Newly Created Netflix Is a Joke Studios

"Two months before they started filming, I got an email from my agent that one of the producers reached out and asked me to send in a tape," Meszaros continues. The actress plays Lisbeth, an outsider who joins the Lions dance team and develops a complicated relationship with Kristina Bogic's Anya.

"All I knew about it was the synopsis, the vague character description and the three scenes that I was given. But that was enough to make me obsessed."

The actress eventually got a callback and did a few chemistry reads. By that point, she was supposed to have been sent the first three episodes but she hadn't been. "I didn't even know how lucky I was," she says. "I feel like the gods were looking down upon me, and it's just ended up being the biggest dream role I could dream up."

Meszaros doesn't have a moment she can point to when she realized she wanted to be an actor. "I honestly remember it as more of a knowing. I was like, 'That is what I'm going to do,'" she says. The actress was fascinated by child actors growing up. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I was just seeing the attention my parents were getting from them. I don't know, there's probably something to unpack there," she says. "It's intuitive for me. I live most things pretty intuitively, and acting feels like an intuitive thing that I enjoy and comes naturally to me."

The tone of the show is so unique and needed right now. What was it like being a part of a project that felt different?

I actually have not processed how just absolutely lucky I am. It's flawless to me. I am always hoping that something that really intrigues me, that I don't know what's going to happen, is going to come along. It's so rare. It's so hard to get those backed. It's truly a blessing.

What were the dance rehearsals like for this?

They were so much fun. It was amazing to be able to build those relationships before filming, even though I guess my character's not everyone's best friend. Our choreographer, Ryan Heffington, is incredible. It was an honor just to work with him. We were so sore. It was long days, and then halfway through, they realized I didn't really need to know the dance, but I did learn it anyway. So I got to sit on the side and have FOMO, which was very Lisbeth for me.

You were getting into character. What was it like finding Lisbeth? I imagine, as an actor, a character like this is exciting for you. What did you hone in on first?

When I auditioned, not really knowing anything, I immediately read it as hilarious. I guess not many people did that. I just found it so inspiring to play and have fun with it, so I wanted to make sure I still brought that into it after I learned more about her. On top of that, the most important thing for me was having empathy for her and really understanding why she does everything that she does. Having a certain level of respect for her because she is really so intelligent and so quick to use things to her advantage. I found that impressive. I found that really admirable, honestly, for a not so admirable human. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Why do you think that's so important for you to find empathy for her?

If I were to just play her scary and manipulative — although I know she does come across as maybe manipulative… I just think it's far more interesting to watch [by not doing that]. Having empathy for a character like that feels important. As far as acting goes, it's not the most noble crusade. That feels like something I can do that's maybe helpful to someone. Rather than manipulative, she's really more of an opportunist, I think. I don't think she planted the seed. She's maybe just watering it. That's A, more fun, B, more real. Because no one is truly good or bad entirely.

How does this role in particular fit into where you are trying to see yourself as an actor?

This is a question that has never been asked to me until recently, and I spent so long trying not to think of where I wanted to be that it's like…

Yeah. I really just trust that the things that are meant for me are going to find me, but I love Mia Goth, which is weird because I don't so much love watching horror, but to play it feels very cathartic, I think. Anything with some grit, anything that's original, I'm happy to do.

You're getting to work with several actors at a very similar point in their career as you're at. What as it been like to do this with the whole group?

That's a big part of why this big group of girls genuinely gets along, which is a miracle. We were all just so grateful to be there all the way through it, and we all wanted to give it our all. Do you have a most memorable experience from shooting it?

articles.title: Recasting the Original Home Alone for 2026
articles.summary: As we put away our pumpkins and string up Christmas lights, it’s the perfect time to rewatch holiday classics like Chris Columbus’s Home Alone. A movie so charming, hilarious, and cozy that it has stood the test of time for more than three decades. While a young Macaulay Culkin absolutely steals the show, it’s the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As we put away our pumpkins and string up Christmas lights, it’s the perfect time to rewatch holiday classics like Chris Columbus’s Home Alone . A movie so charming, hilarious, and cozy that it has stood the test of time for more than three decades. While a young Macaulay Culkin absolutely steals the show, it’s the stacked cast of adult actors that makes the original Home Alone so rewatchable. Rather than phoning it in, world-class talents like Catherine O’Hara and Joe Pesci give it their all, with Pesci delivering one of the best comedic performances of his career, and O’Hara bringing so much heart and soul to the film that the ending still leaves most of us in tears.

The first Home Alone is so perfect that it never needs to be touched or remade again. It feels almost blasphemous to even consider what a recast would look like today. Despite several remake attempts, none have managed to capture the magic of the original. Nonetheless, it’s a fun thought experiment to try and put together a roster that’s even half as iconic. Using a mix of comedians, stars, and underrated talents, the following would be, at the very least, a delightfully unhinged Home Alone remake for 2026.

In Home Alone and Home Alone 2: Lost in New York , Peter McCallister is played by the late American actor John Heard. Heard’s grounded, slightly oblivious father was a fantastic juxtaposition to the absurd situation, and we never stop believing him for a second. Comedian John Mulaney’s energy might not be as grounded, but he's talked at length in his stand-up specials about his religious upbringing, so he could easily play a straitlaced father with nervous energy bubbling up from underneath.

Even better, Mulaney was reportedly scouted for the role of Kevin in the original film, the part that ultimately went to Culkin. According to IndieWire , Mulaney said his parents decided not to let him audition, and lamented that it came on a particularly bad day, right before he was due to get a shot at the doctor’s office. He has also joked that he could never have matched Culkin’s iconic, confident performance as Kevin. But the fact that he was even considered is a sign he could play the character's parent today, and it seems like Mulaney is open to taking on more acting roles these days .

The late comedy legend Catherine O’Hara originated the role of Kate McCallister in Home Alone . Yet, because anyone taking on the part would have major shoes to fill, it might make sense to cast an underrated actor, and Lake Bell could be the perfect sleeper pick. O’Hara’s performance is iconic because she plays it completely straight until she doesn’t. Her airport meltdown is the standout moment, even with the film’s heartfelt ending. Like O’Hara, Bell has a background in character acting with a focus on dry comedy. Her role as Barb Trosper, the mother and wife in Tim Robinson’s cringe comedy series The Chair Company , is perhaps the most fitting on her résumé. 

Bell’s comedic style is deadpan as the character tries to manage her family, get her own business off the ground, and keep her husband in check as he spirals down an absurd rabbit hole. We know Bell can play the mother who is ultimately forced to take the reins in a disastrous situation. Plus, imagining her opposite Mulaney’s neurotic and overly polite Peter is an absolute joy. Bell’s other roles, like Annie Dwyer in No Escape and Carol Solomon in her own film In a World… , have shown she’s also capable of the genuine emotional warmth needed to stick the landing.

Originally played by actor Gerry Bamman, Uncle Frank is easily the most hateable character in the movie. He’s stingy, condescending, and quick to blame Kevin for everything. Bamman’s straight face came to represent everything Kevin hated about his family. Yet, what’s interesting is that Kieran Culkin, brother of star Macaulay Culkin , also appeared in the original Home Alone as Fuller, Kevin’s bed-wetting cousin. Fuller also happens to be Uncle Frank’s son, so it’s easy to see why Kieran could be the perfect choice to play the character and bring some legitimacy to a remake.

Beyond the obvious, Frank wears his sarcasm and contempt on his sleeve, and Kieran is known for that type of delivery. He knows how to say a cruel line casually, as proven by his stint as Roman Roy in HBO’s hit series Succession, where he spends most of his time on screen hurling hilarious insults. Meanwhile, his Wallace Wells in Scott Pilgrim vs. the World shows off the dry, sarcastic side. Though Kieran is famously selective about his roles, there’s no doubt he would make an iconic Uncle Frank.

No one can truly live up to the iconic performance of a young Macaulay Culkin in the original Home Alone , nor his return in Home Alone 2 . Culkin carries the entire movie on his shoulders, balancing a precocious confidence with vulnerability. But that’s why acting newcomer Clark Shotwell would be perfect. Rather than casting a big-name Disney star or nepo baby, the role requires a kid whose charm and talent speak for themselves, while still feeling like a relatable suburban boy. 

Shotwell, a 10-year-old from Dalton Gardens, Idaho, was handpicked by John Travolta to play a younger version of himself in Travolta’s directorial debut, Propeller One-Way Night Coach , which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. It’s Shotwell’s only screen credit so far (though he has plenty of stage experience), but it’s all the proof we need that he could pull off the role. In the film, he plays eight-year-old Jeff, a young aviation enthusiast who travels across the country with his mother. While reviews for the film were mixed, critics praised Shotwell’s performance as genuinely wonderful. All the airplane scenes make it easy to picture what a new version of Kevin might look like if he were to board the wrong flight to New York City.

Originally portrayed by the legendary Joe Pesci, Harry is perhaps the most difficult role to recast. At the time, Pesci was known for playing tough guys, so turning his mob-man persona on its head to play a bumbling robber was a brilliant move. We watch Pesci get blasted, burned, and humiliated, and he sells every bit of the pain, with hilarious G-rated stand-ins for his usual profanities. It’s hard to believe his performance as Harry came out the same year as his Oscar-winning turn in Goodfellas . While Pesci has a small, volcanic energy, Craig Robinson is big, warm, and smooth-talking. Rather than recreate the magic of Pesci’s Harry, Robinson could bring his own spin to the character. 

Instead of being the rational one in the duo, he’d be the charming, suave one who is slowly worn down by his partner’s chaos until he finally loses his cool. Imagine a great scene of Robinson’s Harry being fake-friendly to try and trick Kevin. His role as Doug Judy, the Pontiac Bandit, in Brooklyn Nine-Nine is a perfect example of him playing a charming criminal, and Darryl in The Office proves his excellent comic timing. Having taken many turns as a comedic character actor, he has the range to bring laughs.

Daniel Stern’s original Marv gets perhaps the most belly laughs of the Home Alone runtime. His physical comedy as one half of the Wet Bandits is unforgettable: screaming with a tarantula on his face, screaming with a nail in his foot, and screaming after getting hit in the face with a paint can. His Marv is dim but strangely sweet, growing more unhinged with every ounce of dignity taken from him. Bill Hader, on the other hand, is one of the legendary comedic actors of our time. His usual energy is panicky, often escalating into a meltdown, which would be perfect for a 2026 Marv. 

Hader is at his best when he’s barely holding it together, and his range spans both the cerebral and the physical, so he could bring the same slapstick edge to Marv’s reactions while adding a new edge. In Barry , Hader plays a hitman who is good at the job but bad at being chill , and he voices Fear in Inside Out , so we have plenty of proof of his screaming ability. We also know he’s good at playing dumb and goofy in a duo, thanks to his Officer Slater in Superbad . A fan favorite from SNL , Hader would likely bring more specificity and character-driven comedy than Stern’s almost entirely physical approach. Playing off Robinson’s Harry, the pair could easily be the Wet Bandits of the new age.

Who would you cast in a 2026 Home Alone ? Let us know in the comments below.

articles.content:
CNN Films has acquired " Bernie Taupin : Life, Music, Elton & Me," a documentary about the lyricist behind such durable pop hits as "Your Song," "Tiny Dancer" and Rocket Man," and a longtime collaborator with Elton John. The film will debut on CNN Friday, January 1 at 8 p.m., continuing a tradition at the Skydance network of kicking off a new year with an intimate portrait of an intriguing figure.

“I’ve spent much of my life telling stories, so it’s a curious experience to find yourself the subject of one,” says Taupin, in a statement. “There’s quite a distance between the life I imagined as a kid in Lincolnshire and the one I’ve been fortunate enough to live." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Golden Girls’ and 'Gilmore Girls' Writers' 'Silver Foxes' Screenplay Acquired by Alder Street Productions (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Artificial’ Star Andrew Garfield Recalls Believing OpenAI’s Sam Altman Was ‘Genuinely Great’ and Could Be ‘My Future Best Friend’

Taupin has largely remained out of the spotlight, while John sang his words. The new film features intimate conversations with Taupin, including a rare sit-down with John, who reminisces about their shared history. Director Matthew Miele uses the film to explore Taupin's passions and artistic influences.

“I wanted to explore the imagination behind those words and the singular mind that has helped shape the soundtrack of our lives," Miele says in a statement. “Bernie afforded me rare access to his creative world, revealing an unconventional approach to songwriting in which he paints abstract portraits with words, conjuring images, characters, and emotions that often defy literal interpretation.” CNN Films has previously featured films that explored the lives of Linda Ronstadt and Glen Campbell , among others. "Bernie Taupin: Life, Music, Elton & Me" is directed and executive produced by Matthew Miele. Producers are Derik Murray for Network Entertainment and Stephen McCormack for Reflektor Media. The film is executive produced by Gary Oldman, Charlie Hendon, Greg Zeschuk, Tim Gamble, Brian Gersh, Kent Wingerak, Greg Zeschuk, and Jody Gerson and David Blackman for Polygram Entertainment. CNN Films has acquired television and SVOD rights for the US and Canada.

The controversy stems from Alle Elsker Rasmus , a series that launched on October 26, in which comedian Rasmus Wallbridge was deceived into believing his dream comedy-horror film project was being produced. Well over 100 people were involved with the production, many of whom were in on the prank. Secret cameras filmed Wallbridge as he remained unaware of the true nature of the situation.

What resulted was a Truman Show -style reality series, and Alle Elsker Rasmus met with immediate and severe backlash from the public and the Danish government. It was quickly taken off air and TV2 issued an apology to Wallbridge.

The comedian himself has been relatively relaxed about the prank, which was led by his creative partner, Martin Johannes Larsen, host of Denmark's civilian version of The Traitors . Wallbridge was informed of the show's true nature before it went out and had to power to block its broadcast, according to the network.

Today, TV2 issued a long statement that noted an investigation into Alle Elsker Rasmus was ongoing, having begun earlier this month. The review will "thoroughly examine the process surrounding the creation and publication of the series, and – where relevant – to formulate recommendations for adjusting TV 2’s ethical guidelines," the broadcaster said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Drive Studios , known for making Netflix series Behind Every Man and Prime Video's Girls of Copenhagen , produced the show, and its CEO Kasper Fredshavn has previously issued an apology to Wallbridge. He admitted "the format went too far," but is not commenting further until the end of the review, with which Drive is cooperating.

Results of the review will be presented to the board "within a few weeks," the broadcaster said today. "Regardless of the investigation’s outcome, the overall assessment is already that new leadership is required to spearhead the extensive work of following up on the investigation, rebuilding trust, and overseeing future programming activities."

The broadcaster said it was "clear that trust in TV2’s programming has been challenged" and that it will "face a process of restoration." Its statement added that criticism over the show was "justified" and added: "We must always insist that quality content serves the public, shows consideration for the individuals involved, is rooted in a shared understanding of ethics, and remains relevant to the Danish people."

TV2 paid tribute to Pors as an "outstanding journalist" and a "skilled, respected" media executive, whose work had established the broadcaster as "the leading news broadcaster in Denmark," and called Thirstrup "a passionate advocate for public service broadcasting," and a "skilled and empathetic leader."

Pors took to social media to address her exit. "After nearly an entire professional life – serving in roles ranging from US correspondent, editor-in-chief, and News Director to, most recently, Content Director at TV 2 – it is now time to say goodbye," she wrote.

"Following the series Alle elsker Rasmus , TV2 will install new leadership to rebuild trust in the broadcaster’s programming and its relationships with external producers. That’s just how it is. For now, I am stepping away and have no further comments, but I look forward to new challenges, conversations, and whatever else the future may hold."

Reality television veteran Kristen Doute is channeling her passion for sports and knowledge of pop culture in the brand new podcast Run It Back , in partnership with PODGO.

Co-hosted with Katie DiMento, the video-first show will release new episodes weekly. Run It Back will blend together the intersection of sports and pop culture, creating a space for conversations in sports, entertainment, celebrity culture and everyday life to meet.

"From the NFL, Fantasy drafts and the biggest moments in the worlds of sports to Bravo drama, pop culture’s most viral moments, relationships, style and everything happening online, the hosts bring different perspectives, genuine expertise and plenty of personality to the conversation," a description for the podcast further reads. "The result is an entertaining, accessible and opinionated take on the stories women are talking about, without assuming that sports knowledge and pop culture knowledge have to exist in separate worlds." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Lance Broadway, Pitcher Turned 'Olympus Has Fallen' Actor, Dies at 43 Business New York Knicks Star Josh Hart Inks Two-Book Deal With HarperCollins (Exclusive)

She is also the co-host of the Balancing Act podcast, which was originally branded as Sex, Love…and What Else Matters and launched in 2022.

Now, it’s unclear who will win Season 35 . However, I’m going to make a bold prediction about who I think could take home the mirrorball trophy based on Instagram likes alone.

The couple who could win based on likes is, by a long shot, Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold, which is surprising considering they have the lowest scores. After seeing someone point this out on X following the latest episode to air on the 2026 TV schedule , I decided to do a deeper dive into DWTS ’s Instagram account. Specifically, I was looking at the show’s carousel posts about a couple’s dance, like the one you can see below:

A post shared by Dancing With The Stars #DWTS (@dancingwiththestars)

This set of images for Connor and Rylee’s Jive got 401K views at the time of this writing. Meanwhile, Harry and Jenna’s Paso Doble has 66.8K, Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas’ Samba post has 81.8K, Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach’s Quickstep has 60.4K, Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov’s Salsa has 67.3K and then Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik’s Waltz has 63.5K. These were all of the couples' first dances during the semifinals, and Connor got an overwhelming amount of support in comparison to his competitors.

That continued through the second set of dances too, as Connor and Rylee’s Quickstep got 160K likes. The second highest in likes was Harry and Jenna’s Glee tribute , which got 135K . That was shocking to me considering the Glee of it all.

Now, you might be thinking: But that’s just one episode's numbers. Don’t worry, I went further back. During Grammy Night, Connor and Rylee got the most likes too. The post about their Argentine Tango got 324K likes, with the second-highest-liked post about a single couple’s dance being the one about Tatyana and Jan’s Tango , which got 125K. It’s not even close…

But One Comment Totally Changed My Opinion But wait, let’s take it back one more week. On DWTS’s Disney Night , Connor and Rylee’s Waltz got 390K likes. The next highest-liked post was Mark and Maura’s Peter Pan Jive , which got 126K likes. Once again, it’s not even close.

Horror Movie Night tells the same story too, with the comedian and podcaster bringing in hundreds of thousands more likes than his competitors.

What’s also interesting about this is that the runner-up in terms of likes is always different, while Connor and Rylee consistently bring in the numbers.

Now, I know there are plenty of other posts on that account you could look at; I also assume not all voters on DWTS are active on social media. So I realize this is not the be-all and end-all of who could win. However, I do think it’s very telling. And I’m willing to go so far as to say that it shows us Connor Wood has the following he needs to win the Mirrorball.

So, to see if my wild guess proves to be right (even though I personally want Amber to win ), you can catch the finale of Dancing with the Stars live on Tuesday, November 24 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC or with a Disney+ subscription .

articles.title: Two of Marvel’s Greatest Villains Face Off in Challenges of Doom: Magneto #1 First Look [EXCLUSIVE]
articles.summary: As Marvel villains go, Doctor Doom is one of the best and he’s certainly getting his time to shine right now. He’s about to take center stage on the big screen when he arrives in the MCU with Avengers: Doomsday in theaters next month, but he’s also dominating the pages of Marvel Comics as well. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google As Marvel villains go, Doctor Doom is one of the best and he’s certainly getting his time to shine right now. He’s about to take center stage on the big screen when he arrives in the MCU with Avengers: Doomsday in theaters next month, but he’s also dominating the pages of Marvel Comics as well. He’s fresh off One World Under Doom , and most recently has been testing himself against the biggest names in all of the Marvel Universe in the Challenges of Doom one-shots. July saw him take on Mr. Fantastic, followed by Spider-Man in September, and Doctor Strange in November — but things are just getting started.

Come January, we’re getting a showdown between Doctor Doom and another epic Marvel figure: Magneto. Challenges of Doom: Magneto #1 goes on sale January 6th from writer Al Ewing, artist Annalisa Borgo, and colorist Matt Milla and while we’re already eager to see these two absolute legends face off, consider this an early holiday gift for Doom and Magneto fans everywhere: ComicBook has an exclusive first look.

As is the case with most first looks, we don’t get the dialogue in this scene from Challenges of Doom: Magneto #1 — some things are best experienced without spoilers, after all — but you almost don’t need it to get a quick sense that this is about to be a very tense situation. We see Magneto in a private, emotional moment after the fall of Krakoa when Doom shows up. It’s pretty clear from the images that Doom cares not for Magneto’s private moment but it is also equally clear that Magneto isn’t going to deal with Doctor Doom’s intrusion. The tension between the two is immediate — and maybe it’s possible that Doom has underestimated Magneto. It’s also possible that there’s much more nuance to what’s happening in Challenges of Doom: Magneto #1, something that Ewing himself teased.

“Doom and Magneto are two of the oldest and most successful Marvel villains, and both have spent time as rulers of nations, but despite that, they aren’t so alike,” Ewing told us. “Magneto’s grown more and more multifaceted as time has gone by, a character of infinite nuances and subtleties; Doom I think of more as a honed blade. Victor’s definitely grown over the years, but in a singular direction — closer and closer to the perfect version of DOOM. So, what happens when the knife-sharp force of Doom meets a Magneto struggling under the weight of his emotional complexity? Will Victor try to destroy Max while he’s weak… or is he trying to help?”

The idea that Doom might actually try to help Magneto is a tantalizing one, but even if that does end up being the case, you know there’s going to be conflict as well. Here’s everything you need to know about Challenges of Doom: Magneto #1: “No one, alive or dead, can match the might of DOCTOR DOOM! Victor Von Doom stands apart from them all, particularly as pertains to power — who else can wield so adeptly the very forces of our universe at the level of atoms and electrons? Well… there may be one. The Master of Magnetism, great foe and ally of the X-Men, mutant leader standing tall astride a world that thrums with metallic promise: MAGNETO!”

As was noted previously, the issue is written by Al Ewing with art by Annalisa Borgo and colors by Matt Milla. Final order cut off is November 23rd. The issue goes on sale January 6th.

So, now it’s your turn: who is your favorite Marvel villain? I’m a big Magneto fan personally, but I want to hear your take. Let us know in the comments or on our forum!

Spoilers ahead for The Traitors: New Blood Finale.

I'm counting the days for the next celebrity-filled Traitors cast to get on my TV, but New Blood was a fun watch that really stuck the landing with its finale. At the Fire of Truth ceremony sweaty boy Victor and Traitor Katie were voted off, leaving just Wyatt, Abbey, and Shane in host Alan Cumming 's castle. The latter was recruited via an ultimatum a few episodes ago, meaning he got to take home the full $246,300 prize pot.

While it took until the reunion for Andie to forgive Cirie back in Season 1, I was so impressed by the way that Abbey and Wyatt were able to put their hurt feelings aside and give Shane the support he needed in this emotional moment. I truly can't stop thinking about the two of them walking over to him from opposite sides of the Round Table, and embracing him as he cried.

articles.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Remake Report Gives Update on Missing Game
articles.summary: Last week, the original Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic from BioWare got a new update after 23 years. Now, the remake has resurfaced with a new report. It's been five years since Aspyr Media and Sony Interactive Entertainment announced the remake of KOTOR in 2021. A year later, in 2022, it was revealed […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Last week, the original Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic from BioWare got a new update after 23 years. Now, the remake has resurfaced with a new report. It's been five years since Aspyr Media and Sony Interactive Entertainment announced the remake of KOTOR in 2021. A year later, in 2022, it was revealed that Saber Interactive was moved onto the project in place of Aspyr Media after progress with the latter was unsatisfactory. Since that report, we haven't heard much about the game in either an official or unofficial capacity. That said, a 2028 release window was seemingly teased back in the summer.

We still don't have official, concrete information, but we have a new report from a well-known Star Wars YouTuber by the name of 100% Star Wars . According to the YouTuber, the planned date for the remake's reveal is The Game Awards, which is set to take place on December 10, 2026, live from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Unfortunately, this is the extent of the report.

Interestingly, this report comes alongside a new report about Star Wars Jedi 3 , and this new report notes that the third game in the Star Wars Jedi series will be revealed at The Game Awards , or at least it could be. For one of these reports to be true, the other almost certainly has to be false because there's little chance Star Wars is going to waste two big pops in one night. That said, the Star Wars Jedi series notably has a history with the awards show; Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Remake does not.

All of that said, take all of this information with a grain of salt. Nothing here is official information, and even if it is accurate, it is subject to change, though it would be very late for a game to drop out of a reveal at The Game Awards.

At the moment of publishing, none of the official, implicated parties have commented on this new report, nor the speculation that comes with it. For a variety of reasons, we do not expect this to change, but if it does, we will update the story accordingly.

If Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic Remake is going to release in 2028, as it's been teased, then a reveal in 2027 always seemed more likely; however, there's not a ton of difference between right at the end of 2026 and 2027. Meanwhile, next year is the 50-year anniversary of the sci-fi series, and thus next year is likely going to be riddled with announcements and reveals, which may make a December 2026 reveal better for the remake.
